F. CLIMATE AND AIR QUALITY
San Jose experiences mediterranean climate modified by a significant marine influence from the Pacific Ocean. The principal characteristics of this type of climate are warm, very dry summers, and cool, relatively rainy winters. Average maximum temperatures in January and July are 57.6°F and 81.1°F, respectively. Of the 58 days of measurable rainfall experienced at San Jose in an average year, 49 (84 percent) occur in the six months of November through April.
In the Santa Clara Valley, the prevailing winds during most of the year are northwesterly, originating from the Pacific Ocean and San Francisco Bay. The northwest/southeast orientation of the Santa Clara Valley dictates this northwesterly flow up the valley, which is usually strongest during summer afternoon and becomes weaker at night and in the winter. From May through August, light downslope southeasterly winds occur, more than 25 percent of the time during the late night and early morning hours. From November to February, winds are southeasterly about half of the time, resulting from storms at sea. At the San Jose Civil Defense Weather Station the average annual wind speed is 5.9 mph (2.6 meters/sec.). The Bay Area Air Pollution Control District (BAAPCD) air monitoring station in San Jose has recorded daily average wind speeds as low as 1.4 mph (0.6 meters/sec) during the month of January. Such low wind speeds are associated with poor air pollution dispersal and resultant high ambient pollutant concentrations.
Another important meterological factor related to air quality in the project is the temperature inversion. A temperature inversion layer traps pollutants at low levels, prevents their upward mixing, and leads to impaired air quality. An inversion base height of 2500 feet (760 meters) has over a 50 percent frequency of occurrence in the San Francisco Bay Area Air Basin, which encompasses the project area (BAAPCD, 1968). The inversion layer tends to be lower in the early morning hours (around 4 a.m.), especially in the winter months when it frequently reaches ground level.
